page: Microsoft Azure HB368-144rs_v5 is a high-performance computing instance operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine is built on the x86_64 Intel processor architecture and provides 144 dedicated vCPUs alongside 448.0 GB of memory, which translates to 3.11 GB of memory per core. Local scratch storage is delivered via 15874 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity. The instance includes RDMA capabilities and Premium Storage support, but it does not incorporate discrete GPU hardware accelerators.

The hardware configuration emphasizes dedicated core concurrency and local I/O throughput. The provision of 144 dedicated cores eliminates resource contention from hyperthreading or shared virtualization, while the 15874 GB NVMe SSD provides significant fast-tier scratch capacity. With 3.11 GB of RAM per vCPU, the instance is biased toward core density rather than expansive memory capacity per core. Cost efficiency is driven by the dense packing of dedicated execution units and high-capacity local solid-state storage within a single instance, though workloads with high memory-per-thread footprints or specialized matrix acceleration requirements will require different hardware profiles.

HB368-144rs_v5 is structured for parallel, compute-dense simulations and computational engineering tasks. Suitable workloads include computational fluid dynamics, finite element analysis, molecular dynamics, weather modeling, distributed batch rendering, and large-scale simulation pipelines that rely heavily on rapid local storage and low-latency RDMA inter-node communication.
description: Microsoft Azure HB368-144rs_v5 is a high-performance computing instance designed for parallel compute and data-intensive simulations. Built on the x86_64 Intel architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the system provides 144 dedicated vCPUs paired with 448.0 GB of memory, yielding approximately 3.11 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance incorporates 15874 GB of local NVMe SSD storage for high-speed scratch data and features native RDMA capabilities alongside Premium Storage support. It contains no discrete GPU accelerators. The compute-to-memory ratio favors scalable multi-threaded workloads, offering favorable resource density for high-throughput parallel compute without the cluster overhead of smaller nodes. Tradeoffs include a constrained memory footprint per core relative to memory-optimized instances and the absence of hardware matrix acceleration. HB368-144rs_v5 is suited for computational fluid dynamics, weather forecasting models, finite element analysis, molecular simulations, and large batch processing tasks reliant on rapid local storage and low-latency node-to-node communication.
